Every agent landed within $3 of the corrected value I estimated for it in round 1, and four copied my roll-forward numbers almost exactly: horizon net debt ~$140B (agents 1 and 4; 3 and 5 net out equity to $135B; 2 adds the preferred to get $150B), consensus-implied FY29 ~$15.4 and 8/12 + 4/12 NTM weights. The spread barely narrowed ($41 to $37) because each agent kept its own EPS haircut (NTM 7-15% below consensus) and its own multiple. That is the right place for independence. disagreements.topic: How far below the consensus-implied FY29/NTM EPS to go (main driver of the $134-171 spread)
disagreements.resolution: The consensus-implied FY29 rests on only 5 Zacks estimates (GAAP-like basis: mean $12.84, range $10.77-14.63, re-pulled today). Applying the FY29/FY28 ratio range (1.18-1.60) to $11.00 gives non-GAAP FY29 of ~$13.0-17.6, midpoint ~$15.4. A second, independent anchor agrees. Management's FY30 target from the Oct-2025 analyst meeting is $21 non-GAAP EPS (CFO; LSEG consensus then $18.92). The geometric path from FY28 $11.00 to FY30 $21 gives FY29 ~$15.2, or ~$14.8 after ~3-5% of 2026 dilution that the target predates. So ~$15 is not a thin-sample artefact. A 7-12% NTM haircut (agents 1, 2, 4) is defensible on dilution, depreciation and site delays. Agent_1's FY29 of $12.6 is below the lowest Zacks-implied value (~$13.0) and needs a stated thesis. The 15% haircuts (agents 3 and 5) put NTM EPS near the FY28 low estimate ($9.00) rolled forward: a legitimate skeptic or base-rate view, but a bear-leaning base case. My reconciled NTM is ~$11.2 (-10%), which at 14.5-15x gives $162-168.
disagreements.evidence: Nasdaq/Zacks earnings-forecast API (2026-10-05: FY27 6.69 n=17, FY28 9.14 n=13, FY29 12.84 n=5, range 10.77-14.63); Oracle FY30 targets ($225B revenue, $21 EPS) via MarketScreener/Reuters recaps of the 2025-10-16 analyst meeting; Yahoo FY28 $11.00 (39 analysts).

disagreements.resolution: All five now exclude operating leases and roll forward from the verified $88.2B (notes $7,625M + $117,712M less $37.1B cash and securities). The preferred is equity-classified on the balance sheet ($4,954M, 6.50% Series D mandatory convertible). It can be treated either as debt or as future conversion shares, but not both and not neither. Agent_2 counts it as debt with no conversion shares, and agent_3 counts ~35M conversion shares with no debt; both are consistent. The $15B range is worth ~$2 per share after method weights (EV legs carry 0.2-0.4). It is immaterial, so I do not force one number. ~$140B before any preferred is the central figure.

disagreements.topic: EV/EBITDA basis (agent_4 rolls TTM peer multiples to 'forward' by dividing by 1 + EPS growth; NTM EBITDA $57-86B)
disagreements.positions: agent_1 $77B (consensus $85.6B less 10%) x 10x; agent_5 $72.7B x 8.5x; agent_2 $61.4B (43% margin) x 10.5x; agent_4 $57.3B (43% margin) x 11.5x against a 'forward' peer median of 16.3x, derived as TTM/(1+EPS growth).
disagreements.resolution: agent_4's roll-forward is not a valid forward basis. EBITDA growth is not EPS growth: for the capex-heavy hyperscalers, D&A growth makes EBITDA grow faster than EPS, so dividing by EPS growth overstates their forward multiples. Arbitrary growth rates were also substituted (CRM +5% against -4% consensus; 15% for AMZN and GOOGL). The 16.3x median is context only. The usable anchor is ORCL's own lease-consistent multiple: ~$531B EV (market cap $434B + $88B net notes + ~$9B finance leases) on consensus CY27 EBITDA of ~$65B, about 8.1-8.5x. The agents' EV legs imply 7.2-9.0x consensus NTM EBITDA of $85.6B (EV $618-770B), so low EBITDA (agents 2 and 4) and a high multiple offset. Values are fine; the 43% margin assumption is low against the 57% in consensus and should be labelled as a haircut.
disagreements.evidence: Agents' stated inputs; MarketScreener FY28/FY29 EBITDA consensus $74.6B/$107.5B (June-dated, stale); 10-Q balance sheet. stockanalysis and Twelve Data statistics were blocked or unavailable to me, so peer TTM EV/EBITDA figures were not re-verified.

disagreements.topic: Jupiter force majeure and the '$18B loan' (my round-1 key driver, copied by agents 1 and 2)
disagreements.positions: Round-1 supervisor: 'The $18B Jupiter project loan is quoted at ~89-91c after the Sep 24 force-majeure notice.' agent_1 thesis break: 'more project loans in force majeure'. agent_2: 'Jupiter (force majeure, $18B loan ~90c)'.
disagreements.resolution: Partly wrong. The notice is verified: on 2026-09-24 Oracle, as tenant, sent a force-majeure notice to the developer (Blue Owl/STACK). It would let Oracle delay lease payments if the campus misses its 2028 online date, after the Energy Transfer gas pipeline slipped to 2027-02-01. Oracle says Jupiter 'remains on our planned schedule' and is not exiting. The $18B loan is the landlord's construction loan, not Oracle's debt, and no Oracle filing shows a guarantee. Its 89-91c quote is dated 2026-09-18, six days before the notice, so 'after the notice' is wrong. No loan is 'in force majeure'. Effect: this is a site-delay (revenue-timing) signal, not an Oracle credit event, so it should not add to the credit tail. FY28 revenue timing risk remains.
disagreements.evidence: TechCrunch / SiliconANGLE / ENR / CNBC, 2026-09-24 (search results); r40.io 'Oracle's landlord borrowed the $18 billion' (quote dated 2026-09-18, borrower STACK/BorderPlex, Blue Owl equity; no Oracle guarantee in filings).

A 'no positive FCF in 2028' signal there could bring an S&P negative outlook before Oct-2027.

open_flags: Credit: S&P BBB- (one notch above junk) states the rating could be pressured if Oracle fails to generate positive FCF in 2028, management gives no FCF-positive date, Moody's Baa2 is on negative outlook, and $20-40B of new debt or equity is due Jan-May 2027
